clue.text: Head for back passages in Emsworth Castle

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so this takes the opening letter of back

parts.note: landings are passages or corridors at the top of stairs

explanation.surface: Someone is told where the back corridors lie in a castle at Emsworth.
explanation.walkthrough: In P G Wodehouse's stories Lord Emsworth lives at Blandings Castle; 'Emsworth' looks like the Hampshire town but means the earl.
explanation.definitionFit: Wodehouse's fictional earl, Lord Emsworth, has his ancestral seat at this castle in Shropshire.

clue.text: Weapons: your uncle's stockpiled millions

indicators.note: something stockpiled is held inside, so the millions go inside

parts.note: from the phrase Bob's your uncle, read as Bob's
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: An uncle has been hoarding millions' worth of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob's your uncle' is a British phrase meaning 'there you are'; swapped round, 'your uncle's' gives BOBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombs are explosive weapons.

clue.text: After inane confusion, prepare to shoot musical

indicators.note: puts the shooting order after the jumbled word
the letters of inane are thrown into disorder

parts.note: get your gun is an order to arm yourself ready to fire

explanation.surface: After some silly mix-up, someone is told to ready a weapon for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin's stage show about sharpshooter Annie Oakley is a musical.

clue.text: Very loud direction for Christian soldiers to come up, then pulled back

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: the hymn begins Onward, Christian soldiers
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A loud hymn order is given to Christian troops, who then retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn off means drawn away or withdrawn, the same as pulled back.

clue.text: Part of speech opposing international cooperation?

parts.note: no expresses opposition, as in a no vote
the UN, the United Nations, is a body for countries working together

explanation.surface: Some speech is against countries working together.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun is one of the grammatical word classes, a part of speech.

clue.text: Composer's chosen bad pupil

indicators.note: says the word chosen is in bad shape, its letters disordered

parts.note: Alban Berg studied composition under this composer

explanation.surface: A composer has picked out a poor student.
explanation.walkthrough: The pupil is the composer's own: Berg was one of his best-known students.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Schoenberg was the Austrian composer who pioneered twelve-tone music.

clue.text: Surface area is divided up first

indicators.note: says the cutting comes before the word is, so it leads the charade

parts.note: to cut something up is to divide it

explanation.surface: A surface region is split up before anything else is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical name for skin, the body's outer surface layer.

clue.text: Sweet taken out of drawer for minister

annotationWithheld.clue: Sweet taken out of drawer for minister

clue.text: Mere anarchy follows this result of poor manufacture

definitions.meaning: in Yeats's poem The Second Coming the line is followed by mere anarchy is loosed upon the world
shoddily made goods break into pieces

explanation.definitionFit: Badly made items come to pieces, and Yeats's line precedes 'Mere anarchy is loosed upon the world'.

clue.text: Back with new skills up in Scottish town

indicators.note: in a down clue going up reverses the whole string

parts.note: the rear is the back
arts are skills, as in the arts of war

explanation.surface: Someone returns with fresh talents to a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranraer is a port town in Galloway, south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Hear Romeo's family dog is a flier

indicators.note: tells the solver to take the family name as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: Romeo belongs to the house of Montague in Shakespeare's play
a harrier is a hound bred for hunting hares

explanation.surface: Someone is told that the hound kept by Romeo's family can fly.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird's name is spelt without the E of Shakespeare's Montague's; 'Hear' bridges the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: This harrier is a bird of prey, and any bird is a flier.

clue.text: Formidable oriental novelist

parts.note: stern means severe, forbidding or formidable
E, for eastern, is the usual abbreviation for oriental

explanation.surface: A novelist from the East is said to be intimidating.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne wrote the novel Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: No hat-peg could be this shape

indicators.note: says the letters of these words could be made into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: Something is not a hat-peg, but might have this outline.
explanation.definitionFit: A seven-sided polygon is a geometrical figure, so it is a shape.

clue.text: Old councillor's mind clear: a reform needed

indicators.note: the letters must be formed again, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: An elderly councillor's thoughts are clear, but a reform is called for.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldermanic means relating to an alderman, a senior councillor in former local government.

clue.text: Champion driver, one in a black suit

definitions.meaning: the best golf club, an ace being a champion and a driver being a club
the single-pip card of clubs, a black suit in a pack of cards

explanation.definitionFit: An ace is a one-spot card and clubs is a black suit; ace also means champion and a driver is a club.

clue.text: Respraying car orange? That's some conceit!

indicators.note: spraying again remakes the paintwork, so the letters are remade

explanation.surface: Someone thinks spraying their car orange is a vain idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is overbearing pride, a strong form of conceit.

clue.text: Not fancying a man throwing up defence

parts.note: to be off something is to have lost one's appetite for it

explanation.surface: Someone vomiting has lost their taste for a fellow's defensive play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing up' suggests being sick; here it means building. Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia who built Offa's Dyke, a long earthwork along the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: King Offa ordered the great earthwork on the English-Welsh border built as a defensive barrier.

clue.text: In factual film, all the points sound genuine

parts.note: the four compass points, N, E, W and S

indicators.note: says the word for genuine is to be heard, matching a word of the same sound

parts.note: real means genuine

explanation.surface: A documentary's soundtrack seems authentic throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel was a short cinema film of current events, so factual.

clue.text: Welshman runs hard? Yes, extremely

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
H stands for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: means only the extreme letters of yes, its first and last, are used

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Welshman runs hard and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhys is a common Welsh first name, so it stands for a man from Wales.

clue.text: Always subversive group in pub — here?

definitions.text: Always subversive group in pub — here?

indicators.note: places the first pieces inside the word for the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
a cell is a small secret group of activists

explanation.surface: Conspirators are always plotting in a pub; is this where they meet?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: the underground room of a pub is where such a group would hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's underground storeroom for kegs is the place a secret group could meet unseen.

clue.text: Note about badgers' dens as carrier of disease

indicators.note: the note goes around the dens

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a set or sett is a badger's burrow

explanation.surface: A note concerning badger burrows says they spread disease.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse fly transmits sleeping sickness, so it carries disease.

clue.text: Noisily inflated a bit — horrible

indicators.note: asks for the words to be heard rather than read, matching a phrase of the same sound

parts.note: something that inflated a bit grew some

explanation.surface: Something swelled a little with a loud noise, and the effect was horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome describes something ghastly and repellent, a synonym of horrible.

clue.text: I recall humorist's country

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read from back to front

parts.note: Edward Lear was the humorist of nonsense verse; the 's gives the S

explanation.surface: Someone remembers which country a comic writer came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: The French teacher was encouraging

parts.note: le is French for the
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A French tutor was supportive.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to encourage or entice them, so led on is was encouraging.

clue.text: Scrap of cloth with a Hindu pat tern

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A piece of fabric carries an Indian design.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'pattern' across a line as 'pat tern'.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a melodic framework in Indian classical music, a pattern of notes.

clue.text: Sick arrangement in the minor found by singer

indicators.note: places the minor's word beside the singer's, after it

parts.note: the nightingale is a songbird famed for its singing
a ward is a minor in the care of a guardian

explanation.surface: In a minor key, a singer comes across a layout for the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nightingale ward is the long open hospital ward with beds along both walls, named after Florence Nightingale.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florence-style open hospital ward is a way of laying out beds for patients.

clue.text: Does it pick any number in unlimited series?

definitions.text: Does it pick any number in unlimited series?

indicators.note: puts the letter for any number inside the trimmed word
drops the limits, the first and last letters, of series

parts.note: N is the mathematician's symbol for any number

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a machine chooses numbers from an endless sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: ERIE (series without its first and last letters) holds N. ERNIE is the machine that draws the winning numbers of Britain's Premium Bonds, a state savings lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Premium Bond draw machine selects random numbers, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Fake map to an outstanding US city

indicators.note: read as out-standing, the map and an stand outside the city

parts.note: a chart is a map
LA is Los Angeles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A forged map leads to a remarkable American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is an impostor or fraud, someone fake.
